draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kaloor! This is home to the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, which opened in 1996 with room for 100,000 people. These days it's where Kerala Blasters FC play their home games.
draft.hungryLine: Head toward MG Road for Kerala seafood, or Marine Drive for Malabar snacks.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The JLN Stadium is about a 17 min walk, and St. Antony's Shrine is near JLN Stadium metro station too.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Walk about 23 min to Pachalam and take the Queen's Walkway toward Marine Drive.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Malayalam poet Vylopillil Sreedhara Menon was born in Kaloor.

spots.name: Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium
spots.detail: 17 min walk · Home of Kerala Blasters FC

spots.name: St. Antony's Shrine
spots.detail: Near JLN Stadium metro · People of all faiths come here

spots.name: Pachalam
spots.detail: 23 min walk · Start of the Queen's Walkway

tips.title: Take the metro.
tips.body: Kaloor metro station is a minute away, and J. L. N. Stadium station is a short walk.

tips.title: Join a game.
tips.body: Locals play at the JLN stadium regularly, free of cost.

story.title: A hospital for the city
story.body: Mar Joseph Parecattil founded Lisie Hospital near Kaloor, named after St. Thérèse of Lisieux.

story.title: The big stadium
story.body: The Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium opened, first built for 100,000 spectators. It now seats 41,000.

story.title: Cricket nights
story.body: The stadium hosted international cricket, including 10 One Day Internationals.

story.title: Football takes over
story.body: Kerala Blasters moved in, and football became the stadium's main game.

story.title: The metro arrives
story.body: Kaloor and J. L. N. Stadium metro stations opened on 3 October 2017.

food.name: The Grand Pavilion
food.detail: On MG Road · Try karimeen pollichathu or Alleppey fish curry

food.name: Ojeen
food.detail: Off Marine Drive · Meat-rich Malabar snacks, juices and milkshakes
